title: Confluence Analytics
text:
What we do
Confluence Analytics works with government agencies, catchment management authorities and agricultural groups. Their problems usually involve messy data, highly variable systems and decisions with real consequences.


Scenario and climate adaptation modelling
We model how rivers, wetlands and farms respond to climate change, water management and adaptation options. Our models represent the mechanisms behind each response, so their projections are more reliable outside the historical record.


Data integration and analysis
We bring together gauge records, remote sensing, hydrological model output and field data, and harmonise them into a usable evidence base. We choose statistical methods to fit the question, and we develop new ones when standard methods fall short.


Decision-support tools
We build dashboards, web apps and reproducible software that managers and their analysts can use and extend. Our code is documented and tested, and we release it openly where the client allows.


Ecological risk and condition assessment
We assess condition, risk and benefit for fish, waterbirds, vegetation and other ecological values. Each assessment states its assumptions and the uncertainty around its conclusions.

title: About
text: Confluence Analytics is a Geelong-based consultancy that builds models, analyses and tools for managing water, agriculture and ecosystems. Our clients include government agencies, catchment management authorities and agricultural industry groups.

title: About
text:
How we work
We develop robust models and analyses that target the needs of management decision makers. We work closely with managers so that our outputs are scientifically grounded, interpretable, and push management capabilities forward.
We accentuate scenario modelling and uncertainty. We identify knowledge gaps, assumptions and real environmental variability, so decision makers can see the range of possible outcomes. Our models represent the mechanisms behind ecological and agricultural responses, which makes them more reliable when conditions move outside the historical record.
Our tools follow best practice for reproducible analysis. We document our methods so clients can extend and reuse the work.

title: About
text:
People



Dr Galen Holt, Director
Galen is a quantitative ecologist with more than 15 years of experience applying data analysis and modelling to the management of rivers, wetlands and agricultural landscapes. He holds a PhD in quantitative ecology from the University of Arizona and is a Research Fellow at Deakin University’s Centre for Regional and Rural Futures.
Galen led development of HydroBOT, the toolkit for assessing climate adaptation in the Murray–Darling Basin. He has published 19 peer-reviewed papers and 17 government reports on biodiversity, environmental flows and climate adaptation.


Partners
We bring in specialist partners for each project and build the team around the skills the work needs. We work most often with Prof Rebecca Lester of Black Swan Insights, a freshwater ecologist with more than 20 years of experience at the intersection of environmental science and agriculture. Rebecca has led national programs on drought resilience and agribusiness, and she is accredited in Life Cycle Assessment.

title: About
text:
Software
Galen’s open-source software includes:

HydroBOT assesses ecological, social and economic responses to climate change and adaptation in the Murray–Darling Basin.
hydrogauge provides R access to the water-data services run by Australian states.
eFlowEval assesses ecological outcomes of environmental water from wetland to basin scale.

Galen’s publications are listed on ORCID.
